refuters.argument:
After expanding every Lean definition to primitives, I found no discrepancy between deletionRoot/halfRoots (and the bundles DeletionRootData/HalfRootsData) and the printed maps D_j and H.

DELETION MAP. deletionIndex j i = (i.val : ZMod (n+1)) + (j+1), so P∖j = (μ_{j+1}, …, μ_{j-1}) with child vertex -1 = μ_{j-1} and child vertex 0 = μ_{j+1}; child edge -1 is therefore [μ_{j-1}, μ_{j+1}] with vector P(j+1) − P(j-1) — the printed fused edge, same orientation. deletionRoot j g = fusionIndex j g = if g = j then -1 else ((g-(j+1)).val : ZMod n). For g = j-1, (−2).val = n−1 in ZMod (n+1) casts to −1 in ZMod n, so exactly the two incident roots (incident j g ↔ g = j-1 ∨ g = j, matching 'g ∈ {j-1, j}') map to the fused edge. Otherwise (g-(j+1)).val ≤ n−2 and deletionIndex j of it is g with successor g+1: the retained edge with the same endpoints as E_g = [μ_g, μ_{g+1}], pinned at label level (deletionIndex … = g, g+1), point level (deleteVertex … = P g, P(g+1)), vector level, and with label-level uniqueness. Checked n = 3 (4-vertex parent) by hand: both non-incident roots land correctly (note −1 = 2 in ZMod 3 is handled consistently).

HALF MAP. firstHalfIndex M a i = M + i.val on ZMod ((a−M).val+1) gives λ₁ = (μ_M, …, μ_a); secondHalfIndex M a i = if i = 0 then M else a + i.val on ZMod (n − (a−M).val) gives λ₂ = (μ_M, μ_{a+1}, …, μ_{M−1}); secondHalfEdgeIndex M a i = a + i.val is the parent label of child edge i ≠ 0. d₁ = child edge −1 of λ₁: firstHalf(−1) = P a, firstHalf(0) = P M, vector P M − P a = printed [μ_a, μ_M]. d₂ = child edge 0 of λ₂: secondHalf(0) = P M, secondHalf(1) = P(a+1), vector P(a+1) − P M = printed [μ_M, μ_{a+1}]. contactHalfRoots: g = a ↦ (−1, 0) = (d₁, d₂); (g−M).val < (a−M).val ↦ ((g−M).val, 0), whose first index has parent label M + (g−M).val = g (E_g in λ₁) and second component d₂; otherwise (−1, (g−a).val), first component d₁ and second index with parent label a + (g−a).val = g (E_g in λ₂; (g−a).val = (g−M).val − d < n − d so the cast is faithful and ≠ 0 since g ≠ a). Arcs: {M,…,a−1} = {(g−M).val < contactDistance} and {a+1,…,M−1} = {contactDistance < (g−M).val}, with g = a ↔ (g−M).val = contactDistance; exhaustive and exclusive as printed. Boundary roots g = M, a−1, a+1, M−1 all give the right child edge including the wraparounds firstHalf(−1) = P a and secondHalf(0) = P M.

DOMAIN. Deletion part: all P : LabelledTuple (k+1), k ≥ 3, all j — covers every centre of a simple flat/cusp wall (n ≥ 4). Stating it for every P is acceptable for a definition: the map is purely combinatorial in labels and no bundle clause depends on wall geometry, so the general statement specialises to the printed one without change of meaning. Half part: quantified under WallGerm.VertexEdgeAt M a, which contains ContactSeparated M a (= printed M ∉ {a−1,a,a+1,a+2}); the 3 ≤ k guard excludes no printed instance because ContactSeparated is unsatisfiable for n ≤ 2 and forces n ≥ 5. halfRoots itself is P-independent, as H is.

NON-REFUTING NOTES. (1) HalfRootsData has no explicit uniqueness clause for 'E_g in λ₁/λ₂' (unlike DeletionRootData), but injectivity of firstHalfIndex (accepted HalvesData.first_injective_labels) and secondHalfEdgeIndex_injective already make the parent-label equation determine the child index. (2) The labelling of P∖j with base vertex μ_{j+1} is a representative choice; the source polygon has no distinguished vertex and D_j(g) is characterised by its endpoints, so this is harmless. Neither is a discrepancy with the printed text.
